tasks.question: With the built-in .env support, where are references like ${API_URL} or ${PORT:-3000} inside a value expanded, including the default-value operators?
tasks.search: dotenv expand variable references default value
tasks.verifiedBy: Read lib/DotenvPlugin.js@v5.111.1: expand() walks parsed keys and calls expandValue(value, processEnv, runningParsed), which matches ${...}/$NAME with a regex and handles the :+, +, :- and - operators (defaults), with a self-reference guard.

tasks.question: In module federation, where is a shared module's version checked against the required semver range, both at build time and in the generated runtime code?

tasks.verifiedBy: Read lib/util/semver.js@v5.111.1: satisfy(range, version) evaluates a parsed range against a version; satisfyRuntimeCode(runtimeTemplate) emits the minified `var satisfy = ...` used by ConsumeSharedRuntimeModule (`if (!satisfy(requiredVersion, version))`).

tasks.question: When `CircularModulesPlugin` runs with `hints` enabled, where is the circular-dependency problem built and pushed as a warning, an error or a stats hint?
tasks.verifiedBy: Read @v5.111.1: CircularModulesPlugin.apply creates `new CircularDependenciesWarning(groups, circularGroups.length)` in optimizeDependencies when hints is set, and in afterSeal pushes it to compilation.errors (hints === 'error'), compilation.hints ('stats') or compilation.warnings.

tasks.question: How does webpack avoid building every module re-exported by a side-effect-free barrel file until one of its exports is actually requested? Explain the deferred-request bookkeeping.
tasks.search: lazy barrel side effect free re-export deferred requests
tasks.verifiedBy: Read lib/LazyBarrel.js@v5.111.1: LazyBarrelController.classify records, for sideEffectFree modules, deferrable dependencies (getLazyUntil) in a LazyBarrelInfo keyed by request; LazyBarrelController.request(module, deps) collects forwarded export ids and returns the factory groups to build now, replaying ids recorded before classification.

tasks.question: When splitChunks.maxSize splits a big chunk, how are the modules divided into parts so that adding or removing a file only invalidates a few parts?
tasks.search: split chunks max size deterministic grouping similarity
tasks.verifiedBy: Read lib/util/deterministicGrouping.js@v5.111.1 (used by SplitChunksPlugin for maxSize): nodes sorted by key, getSimilarities computes similarity() of neighbouring keys, Group.popNodes removes too-small nodes, and groups that are too big are split at the minimum similarity between the minSize-bounded left and right areas.

tasks.question: How does webpack decide which modules are part of a synchronous circular import chain, and which of them can observe a live export binding?
tasks.search: circular modules synchronous import cycle strongly connected binding
tasks.verifiedBy: Read lib/CircularModulesPlugin.js@v5.111.1: CycleGraph.build collects sync edges via getSynchronousTarget(connection), records binding reads via isBindingRead, runs an iterative Tarjan SCC (nodeIndex/nodeLowLink/sccStack) and marks members of SCCs larger than one (or self-loops) as synchronous; binding modules are derived from the binding-read edges.
